title: Peer selection and valuation in mergers and acquisitions

rival_explanations: deal-completion incentive: banks rubber-stamp the offer by selecting low-valued peers to make the bidder's offer appear generous and facilitate deal completion (fee collection)
reverse causality: the offer price is already known before peer firms are chosen, so premiums drive peer choice rather than peer choice driving premiums
SIC-code mismatch implies peers are poorly/unrelatedly chosen, i.e. industry is unimportant to peer selection

context.industry_setting: cross-industry (M&A transactions across industries; publicly traded target firms)
context.sample_description: M&A deals with public target firms and deal status completed or withdrawn; hand-collected valuation (comparable companies) data from SEC EDGAR merger filings (DEFM 14A, S-4, SC 14D9) containing target advisors' fairness opinions; deals with deal value >= $1 million, acquirer seeking >= 50% of target, and at least one target financial advisor; SDC data merged with CRSP and Compustat

data_sources.name: Center for Research in Securities Prices (CRSP)
SEC EDGAR merger documents (SEC Form DEFM 14A, S-4, SC 14D9) - hand-collected fairness-opinion comparable companies analysis data
Hoberg and Phillips (2010, 2016) Text-based Network Industry Classifications (TNIC) and product similarity scores
Merger news articles and company SEC Form 10-K filings (peer business-profile information and buyout exit values)
